corpus: mixed human/model final text from earlier sessions
finding: Useful primary personal advantage over base, pooled, donor and uniform remains unresolved under both interval methods. The three model-rival writer intervals favor personal adaptation at zero, but none clears the useful margin and all three crossed writer/prompt intervals include zero. Uniform intervals include zero under both methods. Residual donor and pooled useful advantages remain unresolved under both methods, with all their intervals including zero; residual uniform performance is worse under both. Raw base, pooled and donor useful advantage remains unresolved under both methods. Only raw pooled favors personal adaptation at zero under writer resampling, without clearing the useful margin or surviving crossed resampling at zero; raw base and donor intervals include zero under both methods. Raw sums are worse than uniform under both methods. No useful personal benefit or parity is established.
limits: Mixed human/model training provenance, sparse histories, shared or changed units, one larger-model seed and transferred rank preclude independent human confirmation, backbone or corpus ranking, general personal-learning limits and private-goal inference. Favorable writer intervals at zero do not establish the useful margin or survive crossed resampling at zero. Other matrix cells remain unfinished; failed and unknown predecessors remain separate.
